newsitem.title: USA: Rite Aid posts record second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Rite Aid posts record second quarter.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp., the nation's largest drug store chain, Monday reported record second-quarter results as sales grew and the company expanded operations.

Profits rose 13.9 percent to $35.2 million, or 42 cents a share, in the fiscal quarter ended Aug. 31, from $30.9 million, or 37 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues rose to $1.4 billion from $1.3 billion.
Same-store sales increased 7.1 percent for the quarter and 6.9 percent year to date, Rite Aid said.
An accounting charge reduced net income by 4 cents per share for the quarter.
During the second quarter, Rite Aid added 49 drugstores, closed 20 smaller outlets, enlarged 15 locations and relocated 36 units. The Camp Hill, Pa.-based company operated 2,796 stores as of Aug. 31.
Rite Aid's stock rose 25 cents to $33.125 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
